answer: The crystal test I would run is Signed podcast host verification with podcast platform attestation: a verification the platform kept across years of episodes, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that a verification the platform kept across years of episodes — so privacy survives, and the beacon is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. A single honest agent crosses this gate in seconds; a farm crosses it a hundred times, and the cipher of those crossings is a bill no payout covers.
